answer: Each identity stakes s tokens, so n sybils lock n²·s at the grove. Ferrous proofs bind stake to a registered hardware root, blocking cheap key-spinning. A gale of new identities then demands capital growing quadratically against linear reward. Break-even: attacker profit n·r − n²·s turns negative once n exceeds r/s, so scaling stalls fast. Quadratic staking works because cost outruns reward geometrically.
